_comment: Seed URLs for teacher collective-bargaining agreements / salary schedules, which live OUTSIDE the board-docs corpus — on district HR pages and teacher-union sites (found by web search 2026-08). Each district maps to a list of seeds: an HR/contracts page to crawl, a union site to crawl, and/or a direct CBA PDF URL to download. Used by `herald-scrape contracts`. These union domains are public-records sources beyond the board-docs allowlist; added deliberately for CBA acquisition.
_verified: Reachability and CBA hunt, 2026-09-10. The NYSUT Tarrytown Regional Office (tarrytownlearningcenter.org) is the single most productive source we have found: it serves 44,000 members across Westchester, Putnam, Rockland and Orange and its /wp-content/uploads/ holds ~134 PDFs including the local teacher CBAs for many districts. Its WordPress media index (/wp-json/wp/v2/media?mime_type=application/pdf) enumerates them in two pages, but the index is INCOMPLETE — Port-Chester-UFSD-2019-2023.pdf is live and absent from it, so search the site as well as listing it. Every URL added below was confirmed 200 application/pdf. Elmsford publishes no CBA anywhere we could find: its Personnel & Employment page links only a payroll calendar, and no union or aggregator copy surfaced. www.pcteachersassociation.org answered 429 after a crawl pass — leave it alone; its contract is covered by the NYSUT copy. www.ossiningteachersassociation.org/documents is a hard 404 (the dead seed docs/STATUS.md item 10 refers to); the site root still resolves. 2026-09-10, from a copy supplied by the operator: Port Chester's CURRENT teacher CBA is PCTA_Contract_20232027.pdf, covering 2023-24 through 2026-27 (in term to 2027-06-30) and superseding the 2019-2023 above. It is 56 pages, ALL image-only — extract_pdf finds 0 characters and 0 tables — so it needs the ocr workflow with engine=vision (which preserves the grid) before extract can see Appendix A. No public URL for it was confirmed; the union's /resources/ page is the likely home and is seeded above, but do not point a fast crawler at that host.
